Answer the greeting "Hello, World!".

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/hello-world) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: hello_world.nomi
/// The greeting every program starts with.
pub fn hello() -> String {
    "Hello, World!"
}

// FILE: hello_world_test.nomi
import hello_world.hello

test "Say Hi!" {
    assert hello() == "Hello, World!"
}
```

## How it's written

- `hello` is a function returning the `String`, as the canonical `hello` property is, rather than a `main` that prints it. A value can be asserted; printed output would need `io.replay` to check.
- The string literal is the whole body: a function's last expression is its result.
